evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Aside from the pricing, do you have any other concerns that you also want to discuss on this call?
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer said 'No, just the what it would cost to do the move' — no concerns raised, so N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Rep stated 'that Wednesday is currently open but always changing' but never identified the day as a Best Value Day, never offered a cheaper alternative day, never quantified any savings, never asked about date flexibility.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Rep said 'if you'd like to go ahead, we can definitely help you out with this move' but did not mention rate lock or no deposit. Customer then said 'Let me take your number. I need to call the apartment complex...' — customer did not book; rep did ask for the business but with no rate lock/no deposit framing and no explicit confirmation of booking details on this call.

top_strength: Joanna gathered logistics comprehensively and methodically — floor number, elevator access, walking distances, property type, special items, packing status, and box count — and delivered both core promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) with the 2,000 dollar coverage and no deductible stated clearly.
coaching_note: Step 2's two-concerns question was asked after you had already begun probing (you opened with 'I can see you're planning to do this move on the 28th'), and crucially, you never asked the step 6 final concerns check at the end ('What's still concerning you?'), which cost you the bookend callback to concerns that drives the card. Also, step 7: always lead with rate lock and no deposit *before* the ask for the business to give the customer an easy yes first.
